newsitem.title: USA: Florida smoke case halfway to picking jury pool.
newsitem.headline: Florida smoke case halfway to picking jury pool.

text.p: The judge presiding over a $5 billion class action suit brought by flight attendants against major tobacco firms said on Tuesday he expected the trial would be heard by a panel of six jurors and 10 alternates.

The decision by Dade County Circuit Judge Robert Kaye meant that attorneys, who by Tuesday had taken eight days to select 50 potential jurors, will have to select a pool of up to 100 for the case, Kaye said. That number would allow both sides their legal allotment of juror rejections and a group of 10 extras in case some potential jurors became unavailable by the time the pool is assembled.
"I think you've got to build in some safety factor," said Edward Moss, an attorney representing Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc.

Attorneys had considered about 225 of the original 250 people who received juror questionnaires and were selecting potential jurors at a rate of five to six a day. Attorneys and court officials estimated that jury selection would take most of the next two weeks.

Court officials said they had issued another 100 juror questionnaires to be sure of having enough potential jurors to form the pool. The first of that new group of potential jurors was expected to be questioned by the attorneys starting on Thursday.

The suit, known as Norma Broin vs Philip Morris Cos. Inc., was filed on behalf of 60,000 non-smoking flight attendants seeking as much as $5 billion in damages from tobacco firms for illnesses that attribute to breathing secondhand cigarette smoke on U.S.-based passenger jets.
The trial is expected to take up to three months after jury selection is completed.
